name: Ginger
description: The universal warming root — fresh in chai, dried in every tradition's pharmacy.

tcm.note: Fresh is warm; dried (gan jiang) is hot.

ayurveda.note: 'The universal medicine' — strongly ushna.

histamine.note: Not just safe — traditionally considered histamine-friendly.

name: Garlic
description: Pungent bulb at the base of savory cooking everywhere.

histamine.note: Well tolerated.

name: Turmeric
description: Golden root powder in nearly every desi dish.

histamine.note: Well tolerated; sometimes suggested as mast-cell-calming.

name: Cumin
description: Earthy seed; the digestive workhorse spice.

ayurveda.note: Mildly heating but pitta-tolerable — the gentle digestive.

histamine.note: Well tolerated.

name: Coriander seed
description: Citrusy seed — the rare spice every tradition calls cooling.

ayurveda.note: The classic cooling spice; dhania water for pitta.

histamine.note: Well tolerated.

name: Fennel seed
description: Sweet anise-y after-meal seed.

tcm.note: TCM calls fennel warming (dispels cold) — the opposite of the desi view.

ayurveda.note: THE cooling digestive — saunf sharbat for summer.

histamine.note: Well tolerated.

name: Fenugreek seed
description: Bitter golden seed; hilba tea and methi tempering.

unani.note: Textbook garam — hilba is a winter drink.

histamine.note: Well tolerated.

name: Black pepper
description: The default table heat.

histamine.note: Small culinary amounts are fine for most.

name: Red chili
description: Dried red heat, whole or powdered.

histamine.note: Capsaicin is a liberator — a double hit when flaring.

name: Green chili
description: Fresh sharp chili chopped into everything desi.

histamine.note: Same capsaicin caution as red chili.

name: Cinnamon
description: Sweet warming bark.

tcm.note: Rou gui is one of TCM's great interior-warming herbs.

histamine.note: Mild liberator; cassia more than true cinnamon.

name: Green cardamom
description: Perfumed pod of chai and gahwa.

ayurveda.note: Green elaichi is called tridoshic/mildly cooling by some, heating by others; black cardamom is unambiguously heating.

unani.note: Desi folk treat chhoti elaichi as thandi (mouth-cooler); hakims vary.

histamine.note: Well tolerated.

name: Clove
description: Intense numbing flower bud.

histamine.note: Culinary amounts fine.

name: Nutmeg
description: Warm sweet grating spice; sedative in large doses.

ayurveda.note: Given in warm milk for sleep.

histamine.note: Pinch amounts fine; large doses are toxic regardless.

name: Saffron
description: Golden threads of biryani, kheer, and Persian tea.

tcm.note: TCM's fan hong hua moves blood; nature listed neutral-ish.

ayurveda.note: Mildly ushna yet tridoshic — given in milk.

unani.note: Zafran is classically garam and mood-lifting.

histamine.note: Thread amounts fine.

name: Mustard seed
description: Popping tempering seed and the source of sarson oil.

histamine.note: Prepared mustard condiment is worse (vinegar); seeds mostly fine.

name: Ajwain / carom
description: Thyme-sharp digestive seed for gas and heaviness.

tcm.note: Not a standard TCM item; inferred.

histamine.note: Well tolerated.

name: Kalonji / black seed
description: Tiny black seed of naan and Prophetic medicine.

tcm.note: Not a standard TCM item; inferred.

unani.note: Habbat al-barakah — central to Unani/Prophetic practice.

histamine.note: Well tolerated; sparse formal data.

name: Asafoetida (hing)
description: Pungent resin pinch that de-gasses dal.

histamine.note: Pinch amounts fine; often cut with wheat flour (gluten note).

name: Star anise
description: Licorice-sweet star of Chinese braises and biryani.

histamine.note: Well tolerated.

name: Sichuan pepper
description: Numbing-tingling peppercorn of mala cooking.

ayurveda.note: Not classical; inferred.

histamine.note: Sparse data; pungent spices warrant caution when flaring.

name: Curry leaves
description: Aromatic tempering leaf of South Asian kitchens.

tcm.note: Not classical; inferred.

ayurveda.note: Sources split between mildly cooling and mildly heating.

histamine.note: Well tolerated.

name: Garam masala
description: The 'warming blend' — cinnamon, clove, cardamom, pepper, cumin.

tcm.note: A blend of warming spices by definition.

ayurveda.note: Literally named 'hot spice mix'.

histamine.note: Depends on the blend; chili-containing versions score higher.

name: Mint
description: The chutney-and-tea herb every tradition reaches for in summer.

tcm.note: Bo he releases heat from the surface.

histamine.note: Well tolerated.

name: Cilantro / coriander leaves
description: The garnish leaf of three cuisines.

tcm.note: Leaf cools; TCM also uses it to vent rashes.

histamine.note: Well tolerated.

name: Basil
description: Sweet Italian basil to sacred tulsi — all warming.

ayurveda.note: Tulsi is explicitly heating — a cold-and-flu herb.

histamine.note: Well tolerated.

name: Parsley
description: The bulk green of tabbouleh.

tcm.note: Thinly documented.

ayurveda.note: Mildly heating, diuretic.

unani.note: Baqdunis leans garam in Unani sources.

histamine.note: Well tolerated.

name: Dill
description: Feathery herb of fish, raita, and Egyptian shibint.

histamine.note: Well tolerated.

name: Sumac
description: Tangy crimson powder over fattoush and mashawi.

tcm.note: Not classical; inferred from sour-astringent use.

ayurveda.note: Astringent-sour; thin documentation.

unani.note: Summaq is classically cold — used to settle heat and gut.

histamine.note: Sparse data; sour condiments warrant mild caution.

name: Za'atar (blend)
description: Thyme-sesame-sumac blend on manakish and labneh.

tcm.note: Blend; thyme base is warming.

unani.note: Wild thyme (za'atar herb) is classically garam.

histamine.note: Generally fine; sesame component noted separately.

name: Sesame seeds
description: Oil-rich seed; tahini, til laddu, and zhi ma jiang.

tcm.note: Black sesame is the warmer, kidney-tonic form.

ayurveda.note: Til is textbook heating — a winter laddu.

histamine.note: Also a major true allergen (separate from histamine).

name: Basil seeds (sabja)
description: Gel-forming seeds of falooda and summer sharbats.

tcm.note: Not classical; inferred from use.

ayurveda.note: Curious flip: the basil plant is heating, its seeds are used as coolers.

unani.note: Tukh malanga is a classic garmi remedy.

histamine.note: Sparse data; traditionally very gentle.

name: Soy sauce
description: Fermented salty backbone of Chinese cooking.

tcm.note: Listed cool/cold in TCM food lists.

ayurveda.note: Fermented + salty; not classical.

unani.note: Not classical; fermented foods lean garam.

histamine.note: Long fermentation = one of the highest-histamine condiments.

name: Vinegar
description: Sour preserving liquid; sirka of Unani texts.

ayurveda.note: Strongly sour = ushna.

unani.note: Classical Unani calls sirka cold — disagrees with Ayurveda/TCM.

histamine.note: Clear spirit vinegar ~1; wine/balsamic vinegars are a 3.

name: Honey
description: The blessed sweetener of every tradition's medicine chest.

tcm.note: Neutral-moistening in TCM.

ayurveda.note: Ushna — and never to be cooked, per classical rule.

histamine.note: Generally well tolerated in modest amounts.

name: White sugar
description: Refined cane sugar.

tcm.note: White sugar neutral-ish; rock sugar considered cooling.

ayurveda.note: Sweet = cooling; old texts prefer unrefined forms.

unani.note: Cheeni is thandi — vs garam gur.

histamine.note: No histamine issue (other health caveats apply).

name: Jaggery (gur)
description: Unrefined cane sugar block; winter sweets.

tcm.note: Brown/red sugar (hong tang) is TCM's warming sugar for cramps and cold.

unani.note: Gur is textbook garam — the classic winter sweet vs thandi cheeni.

histamine.note: Less refined; trace amines possible. Sparse data.

name: Chocolate / cocoa
description: Cocoa in all its forms — and a major histamine offender.

tcm.note: Not classical; modern sources call it warming-damp.

ayurveda.note: Stimulant, bitter-pungent.

histamine.note: Liberator AND DAO-blocker — a top flare trigger.

name: Mustard oil
description: Pungent yellow oil, smoked till it stops biting — the North Indian and Bengali frying fat.

tcm.note: The mustard family is hot and dispersing in the Chinese reading.

ayurveda.note: Sarshapa taila is ushna and tikshna — the classic winter massage and cooking oil, kapha- and vata-reducing.

unani.note: Garam-khushk; rubbed on for cold, stiffness and chest congestion.

histamine.note: Pure fat, so effectively nothing — the pungency is not a histamine mechanism.

name: Sesame oil
description: Nutty oil from til — toasted and dark for Chinese cooking, pale and raw for South Indian.

tcm.note: Zhi ma you is warm and moistening; the toasted kind is a finishing oil, not a frying one.

ayurveda.note: Tila taila is ushna and the single most-used oil in Ayurveda — the default base for abhyanga.

unani.note: Garam-tar, warming and strengthening to the joints.

histamine.note: Pure fat; low. Sesame itself is a common allergen, which is a different mechanism.

name: Coconut oil
description: Solid below room temperature — the frying fat and hair oil of the coast.

tcm.note: Not part of the classical Chinese record.

ayurveda.note: Narikela taila is shita — the standard cooling oil, poured on the scalp against heat.

unani.note: Thanda-tar, the counter-oil to sarson: used in the south and in summer.

histamine.note: Pure fat; among the safest cooking fats.

name: Olive oil
description: Green, peppery and poured raw over everything on the Levantine table.

tcm.note: A Mediterranean fat with no classical Chinese entry.

ayurveda.note: Not classical; oils in general are read as ushna and unctuous.

unani.note: Zait zaytoon is har-ratab and among the best-documented tonics in the Unani record.

histamine.note: Pure fat; specifically recommended on histamine-restricted diets.

nutrition.highlight: poured raw, not just cooked in

name: Sunflower oil
description: The neutral refined oil most kitchens actually fry in.

tcm.note: A modern refined product with no classical entry.

ayurveda.note: Oils are read as ushna; refining strips the character that would place it more precisely.

unani.note: Garam by the general rule for oils, not by any specific record.

histamine.note: Low. Repeatedly reheated frying oil is a separate problem.

name: Palm oil
description: Cheap semi-solid fat behind most packaged biscuits and fried snacks.

tcm.note: No classical entry; heavy saturated fats are read as damp-forming.

ayurveda.note: Ushna and very guru — heavy and slow to digest.

unani.note: Garam and heavy; outside the classical record.

histamine.note: Low as a fat.

name: Bay leaf
description: Dropped whole into the oil at the start and fished out at the end.

tcm.note: An aromatic warming leaf, in the cinnamon family.

ayurveda.note: Tejpatra is ushna, katu and deepana — a digestive stimulant.

unani.note: Garam-khushk, carminative and warming to the stomach.

histamine.note: Low; used in tiny amounts and removed.

nutrition.highlight: in at the start, out at the end

name: Oregano
description: Dried Mediterranean herb — pizza's defining smell.

tcm.note: Aromatic and dispersing; not in the classical record.

ayurveda.note: Katu and aromatic, read as ushna.

unani.note: Garam-khushk; the wild oregano of the Levant is a documented carminative.

histamine.note: Low.

name: Thyme
description: Small pungent leaves — the backbone of the zaatar blend.

tcm.note: Aromatic and warming; outside the Chinese record.

ayurveda.note: Read as ushna from its pungency.

unani.note: Hasha is well documented as garam-khushk, given for cough and cold stomachs.

histamine.note: Low.

name: Rosemary
description: Woody needles with a resinous, pine-like bite.

tcm.note: Aromatic and dispersing; no classical entry.

ayurveda.note: Ushna by its pungency and aroma.

unani.note: Iklil al jabal is garam-khushk in the Arab record, given for memory and cold headaches.

histamine.note: Low.

name: Sage
description: Soft grey-green leaves — brewed as tea across the Levant, fried in butter in Europe.

tcm.note: Not classically listed; aromatic and warming.

ayurveda.note: Read as ushna.

unani.note: Maryamiya is garam-khushk and a standard Levantine tea for the stomach and for cramps.

histamine.note: Low.

name: Lemongrass
description: Fibrous stalk bruised into curries and teas for its citrus oil.

tcm.note: Aromatic and surface-releasing — used against early chills.

ayurveda.note: Ushna and katu, a diaphoretic used in fever teas.

unani.note: Garam; the regional record is thin.

histamine.note: Low.

name: Thai basil
description: Purple-stemmed anise-scented basil, thrown in at the end of a stir-fry.

tcm.note: Jiu ceng ta is warm and dispersing, added off the heat to keep its oils.

ayurveda.note: The tulsi family is firmly ushna and katu.

histamine.note: Low.

name: Kaffir lime leaf
description: Glossy double leaf, torn into soups for a sharp citrus perfume.

tcm.note: Aromatic and qi-moving; the Chinese record is thin on it.

ayurveda.note: Read as ushna from its aroma.

histamine.note: Low; used whole and removed.

name: White pepper
description: The same berry as black pepper, hulled — earthier, and less sharp.

tcm.note: Bai hu jiao is hot; it warms the middle and stops cold-type pain, and is used more freely than black in Chinese cooking.

ayurveda.note: Maricha is ushna and tikshna whichever way it is processed.

unani.note: Garam-khushk, in the same degree as black pepper.

histamine.note: Low in normal amounts; strong spices can irritate independently of histamine.

name: Long pepper
description: Small dark catkin, hotter and sweeter than peppercorn — a classical drug more than a kitchen spice.

tcm.note: Bi ba is hot and warms the middle burner against cold pain.

ayurveda.note: Pippali is ushna and one third of trikatu — the classical rasayana for the lungs and gut.

unani.note: Dar filfil is garam-khushk in a high degree.

histamine.note: Low; taken in very small amounts.

name: Mace
description: The lacy red web around the nutmeg seed — finer and sharper than the nut.

tcm.note: Read with nutmeg, which is warm and binding.

ayurveda.note: Jatipatri is ushna and katu, used in garam masala for exactly that reason.

unani.note: Garam-khushk; a warming aromatic for the stomach and heart.

histamine.note: Low in culinary amounts.

name: Allspice
description: One berry that tastes of clove, cinnamon and nutmeg at once — the base of Levantine bahar.

tcm.note: A new-world spice with no classical Chinese entry.

ayurveda.note: Ushna by its aroma and pungency; not classical.

unani.note: Garam-khushk; absorbed into Levantine practice as a warming digestive.

histamine.note: Low in culinary amounts.

name: Paprika
description: Ground dried sweet peppers — colour first, heat a distant second.

tcm.note: Read with the chilli family, milder.

ayurveda.note: Ushna like all the capsicums, if gently so.

unani.note: Garam, though far below red chilli in degree.

histamine.note: The dried capsicums are flagged as liberators — paprika and chilli powder both.

name: Caraway
description: Curved seed with a sharp anise-and-rye note, often confused with cumin.

tcm.note: Aromatic and carminative; thin Chinese record.

ayurveda.note: Ushna and deepana, in the cumin family.

unani.note: Karawya is garam-khushk and a standard Unani carminative.

histamine.note: Low.

name: Anise seed
description: Sweet liquorice-scented seed, brewed as yansoon tea for a settled stomach.

tcm.note: Read with the fennel and star-anise group, which is warm.

ayurveda.note: Ushna and deepana, though desi usage treats aniseed drinks as cooling.

unani.note: Yansoon is garam in the Arab record, given for colic and wind.

histamine.note: Low.

name: Poppy seed
description: Tiny white or blue seeds ground into a paste to thicken korma and posto.

tcm.note: The seed is not the classical drug; thin record.

ayurveda.note: Khaskhasa is shita, heavy and mildly sedating — a cooling thickener, unusually for a spice.

unani.note: Khashkhash is barid-ratab and given to induce sleep — one of the few thanda items in the masala box.

histamine.note: Low.

name: Galangal
description: Ginger's harder, sharper relative — piney rather than hot.

tcm.note: Gao liang jiang is hot and warms the stomach against cold pain — stronger than fresh ginger.

ayurveda.note: Kulanjana is ushna and katu, in the ginger group.

unani.note: Khulanjan is garam-khushk in a high degree, a classical stomach warmer.

histamine.note: Low.

name: Amchur
description: Unripe mango dried and ground — sourness without any liquid.

tcm.note: Follows green mango; no Chinese entry.

ayurveda.note: Amla-rasa and ushna, like the unripe fruit it is made from.

unani.note: Garam and drying, though the fresh green mango is read the other way.

histamine.note: Concentrated sour fruit — the same flag as green mango, more so for being dried.

name: Anardana
description: Dried wild pomegranate seeds, ground for a dark fruity sourness.

tcm.note: Follows pomegranate, which TCM reads as warm.

ayurveda.note: Dadima is shita and grahi — sour but cooling, the same exception amla makes.

unani.note: Anar is thanda in desi usage; drying the seed makes it drying too.

histamine.note: Low; used in small amounts.

name: Chaat masala
description: Sour-salty blend built on black salt and amchur — dusted over fruit, eggs and chaat.

tcm.note: A compound blend; read from its warming aromatic base.

ayurveda.note: Ushna: cumin, ajwain, black pepper and amchur are all heating.

unani.note: Garam-khushk, an appetiser blend by design.

histamine.note: Amchur-based and sour — worth knowing, since it is dusted on last and often forgotten.

name: Five-spice powder
description: Star anise, cassia, clove, fennel and Sichuan pepper, ground together.

tcm.note: Every one of its five components is warm or hot — a deliberately warming blend.

ayurveda.note: Ushna by all its parts.

histamine.note: Low in culinary amounts.

name: Baharat
description: The Levantine warm-spice blend — pepper, allspice, cinnamon, clove and more.

tcm.note: Read from its components, all of which are warming.

ayurveda.note: Ushna throughout — the Arab counterpart to garam masala.

unani.note: Garam-khushk; every component is garam in the Unani record.

histamine.note: Low in culinary amounts.

name: Tahini
description: Ground hulled sesame — the backbone of hummus and every mezze sauce.

tcm.note: Sesame is warm and moistening; the paste concentrates it.

ayurveda.note: Tila is ushna, guru and snigdha — heating and heavy.

histamine.note: Low fresh. It goes rancid quietly, and rancid fat is its own problem.

name: Miso
description: Soybeans fermented with koji for months into a deep salty paste.

tcm.note: Long-fermented and salty; read as warming and descending.

ayurveda.note: Fermented and salty, so ushna.

unani.note: Garam by its ferment and salt; outside the classical record.

histamine.note: A months-long soy ferment — one of the highest-histamine foods there is, alongside soy sauce.

name: Fish sauce
description: Anchovies salted and left to break down for a year — pure savoury depth.

tcm.note: Salty and long-fermented; read as warming.

ayurveda.note: Fermented fish is ushna and outside classical vegetarian practice.

histamine.note: Fermented fish is the single worst combination on this scale — fish plus a year of ferment.

name: Oyster sauce
description: Thick dark sauce of reduced oyster extract, sugar and salt.

tcm.note: A modern compound sauce; oysters themselves are neutral-cool.

ayurveda.note: Read as ushna from its salt and shellfish base.

histamine.note: Shellfish extract, aged and salted — high, and it is in almost every stir-fry.

name: Hoisin sauce
description: Sweet, thick, garlicky fermented soybean sauce — what duck pancakes are painted with.

tcm.note: Sweet, fermented and garlicky; read as warming.

ayurveda.note: Fermented and sweet-pungent, so ushna.

histamine.note: Fermented soy base, like soy sauce and miso.

nutrition.highlight: what duck pancakes are painted with

name: Gochujang
description: Fermented chilli and rice paste — sweet, savoury and slow-burning.

tcm.note: Chilli plus a long ferment — hot by both routes.

ayurveda.note: Strongly ushna: katu and fermented together.

histamine.note: Fermented and chilli-based — it carries both mechanisms at once.

name: Harissa
description: North African paste of roasted chillies, garlic, caraway and oil.

tcm.note: Chilli-based, so hot; no Chinese entry.

ayurveda.note: Ushna and tikshna — chilli, garlic and caraway together.

histamine.note: Chilli liberator; jarred versions often carry vinegar and preservatives too.

name: Ketchup
description: Sweetened, vinegared tomato concentrate — the default table sauce almost everywhere.

tcm.note: Follows tomato, which is cool, though the sugar and vinegar complicate it.

ayurveda.note: Sour and fermented-vinegared, so ushna despite the cooling fruit.

unani.note: Garam by its vinegar; no classical entry.

histamine.note: Concentrated tomato plus vinegar — tomato alone is already a SIGHI 3, and this is tomato reduced.

name: Mayonnaise
description: Egg yolk and oil emulsified with vinegar or lemon.

tcm.note: A modern emulsion; egg is neutral, oil is warming.

ayurveda.note: Guru and ushna — oil and egg with a sour agent.

histamine.note: Vinegar-set and egg-based; both raise it above a plain oil.

name: Apple cider vinegar
description: Cider fermented twice — to alcohol, then to acid.

tcm.note: Cu (vinegar) is warm and astringent, and moves stagnant blood.

ayurveda.note: Shukta is ushna and strongly pitta-aggravating — sour and fermented together.

unani.note: Sirka is garam despite feeling sharp and cooling on the tongue.

histamine.note: SIGHI names apple cider vinegar with distilled white among the tolerated vinegars — it is wine and balsamic vinegars that rate badly, not this one.

name: Balsamic vinegar
description: Grape must aged in wood for years into a sweet dark syrup.

tcm.note: Read with vinegar, which is warm and blood-moving.

ayurveda.note: Sour, sweet and long-fermented — firmly ushna.

histamine.note: Years of barrel ageing on a grape base — vinegar and wine problems compounded.

name: Rice vinegar
description: Mild pale vinegar from fermented rice — the gentlest of the family.

tcm.note: Cu is warm, sour and astringent; it enters the liver and moves stagnation.

ayurveda.note: Shukta is ushna, whatever grain it comes from.

unani.note: Sirka is garam-khushk in the Unani record.

histamine.note: Mild and not wine-based, so it sits with the tolerated vinegars rather than with balsamic — it is often suggested as the substitute.

name: Maple syrup
description: Boiled-down maple sap — mineral-sweet, with a faint woodiness.

tcm.note: Not classically listed; sweet syrups are read as tonifying and damp-forming.

ayurveda.note: Madhura rasa is generally shita — closer to sugar than to honey, which is ushna.

unani.note: Garam-tar by the general rule for concentrated sweets.

histamine.note: Low; not fermented, unlike honey's more complicated position.

name: Date syrup
description: Dates reduced to a dark treacle — poured over tahini, or into sweets.

tcm.note: Follows the date, which is warm and tonifying.

ayurveda.note: Concentrated dates are ushna and building — a winter sweetener.

unani.note: Dibs is garam-tar, a classical strengthening food of the Arab table.

histamine.note: Concentrated dried fruit, so it sits with dates and raisins rather than with plain sugar.

name: Salt
description: Plain sodium chloride — the one seasoning in every kitchen on earth.

tcm.note: Salt is classified cold and descending in TCM, entering the kidney; it softens hardness and moves downward.

ayurveda.note: Lavana rasa is ushna, tikshna and the great appetiser — one of the six tastes, and the one that drives pitta.

unani.note: Namak is garam-khushk in Unani, drying and dissolving — used to cut phlegm.

histamine.note: None in itself. Salt is what preserves the cured and fermented foods that rate badly, but the salt is not the histamine.

name: Black salt
description: Sulphurous pink-grey rock salt — the smell is the point, and it is why chaat tastes of chaat.

tcm.note: Read with salt; the mineral content does not change its descending nature.

ayurveda.note: Saindhava-family lavana, ushna and deepana, and classically the lightest salt on digestion.

unani.note: Garam-khushk; given for wind and indigestion, which is its main hakimi use.

histamine.note: None in itself.

name: Rock salt
description: Unrefined mined salt — the only salt allowed on Hindu fasting days.

tcm.note: Read with salt.

ayurveda.note: Saindhava is the one lavana classically called shita rather than ushna, and the only one said not to aggravate pitta.

unani.note: Garam-khushk, though gentler than table salt in hakimi usage.

histamine.note: None in itself.

name: MSG
description: Crystallised glutamate — pure savouriness, and nothing else.

tcm.note: A twentieth-century isolate with no classical entry.

ayurveda.note: No classical entry; lavana-adjacent and read as ushna.

histamine.note: Glutamate is not histamine, but it is a common trigger for the same people — and SIGHI flags it as one of the other biogenic amines to watch.

name: Achar
description: Fruit or vegetable cured in salt, oil and spice for weeks — a spoonful to the side of the plate.

tcm.note: Salted, soured and oil-cured; hot and stimulating.

ayurveda.note: Amla-rasa plus lavana plus ushna spices — classically said to aggravate pitta and rakta.

unani.note: Garam-khushk; the reason it is eaten in small amounts and avoided in skin complaints.

histamine.note: Weeks of salt fermentation — one of the highest things on a desi plate, and the easiest to forget because the portion is small.

name: Kimchi
description: Napa cabbage lacto-fermented with chilli, garlic and salted shrimp.

tcm.note: Chilli and garlic over a fermented base — hot and dispersing.

ayurveda.note: Ushna and tikshna: soured, salted and chilli-hot together.

histamine.note: A deliberate live lacto-ferment with chilli and salted seafood in it — about as high as a vegetable gets.

name: Sauerkraut
description: Shredded cabbage left in its own brine until it sours.

tcm.note: Cabbage is cooling; the ferment adds a warming sourness.

ayurveda.note: Soured, so ushna, though the cabbage beneath is shita.

unani.note: Garam by ferment; outside the classical record.

histamine.note: The textbook high-histamine vegetable — often the single worst thing in an otherwise careful meal.

name: Pomegranate molasses
description: Pomegranate juice boiled down to a dark, sharply sour syrup.

tcm.note: Follows pomegranate, which TCM reads as warm; reduction concentrates it.

ayurveda.note: Dadima is shita even when sour — the same exception amla makes.

unani.note: Anar is thanda in the Unani record; boiling it down makes it drying.

histamine.note: Very concentrated and sour — the flavour that makes muhammara and fattoush is also what rates them.

name: Tamarind paste
description: Tamarind pulp strained and reduced — sourness in a jar.

tcm.note: Follows tamarind, which is cool and fluid-generating.

ayurveda.note: Amlika is amla-rasa and ushna, classically pitta- and rakta-aggravating.

unani.note: Tamr hindi is barid in Unani and given against bilious heat — the reverse of the Ayurvedic reading.

histamine.note: Concentrated sour fruit; a jarred paste is stronger again than the pulp.

name: Sriracha
description: Fermented red chilli, garlic, vinegar and sugar, blended smooth.

tcm.note: Chilli and garlic, fermented — hot on every count.

ayurveda.note: Ushna and tikshna throughout.

histamine.note: Fermented chilli plus vinegar — both mechanisms in one bottle.

name: Prepared mustard
description: Mustard seed ground with vinegar into a spreadable paste.

tcm.note: Read with mustard seed, which is warm and dispersing.

ayurveda.note: Sarshapa is ushna and tikshna.

histamine.note: The vinegar carries it; the seed itself is low.

name: Kasuri methi
description: Fenugreek leaves dried and crushed between the palms over a finished dish.

tcm.note: Read with fenugreek, which is warm and drying.

ayurveda.note: Methi is ushna and deepana; drying concentrates it.

unani.note: Garam-khushk, and the smell that makes a butter chicken taste right.

histamine.note: Low; used in pinches and added off the heat.

name: Rose water
description: Distilled rose petals — a splash into sweets, drinks and rice.

tcm.note: Rose is cool and qi-moving in the Chinese reading, calming to the liver.

ayurveda.note: Gulab is shita and the classical pitta-pacifier — which is why it goes into summer drinks.

unani.note: Thanda-tar; gulqand and gulab sharbat are standard Unani coolers.

histamine.note: Very low.

nutrition.highlight: the smell of a summer drink

name: Kewra water
description: Pandanus flower distillate — a few drops perfume a whole pot of biryani.

tcm.note: No classical Chinese entry; aromatic distillates read as cooling.

ayurveda.note: Ketaki is shita and used in the same place as rose.

unani.note: Thanda-tar; a cooling perfume for rice and sweets.

histamine.note: Very low; used in drops.

name: Dried mint
description: Mint dried and crumbled — stirred into laban, sprinkled over soup.

tcm.note: Bo he is cool and surface-releasing; drying does not change that.

ayurveda.note: Pudina is shita and pitta-pacifying.

unani.note: Thanda-khushk; the standard Levantine finish for yogurt dishes.

histamine.note: Very low.

name: Curry powder
description: The British-Indian catch-all blend — turmeric-heavy, and not a thing any desi kitchen keeps.

tcm.note: Read from its components, which are warming throughout.

ayurveda.note: Ushna: turmeric, cumin, coriander and chilli together.

histamine.note: Low in culinary amounts.

name: Sambar powder
description: Roasted dals and chillies ground with coriander — the South Indian house blend.

tcm.note: Roasted and chilli-forward.

ayurveda.note: Ushna and deepana throughout.

histamine.note: Low in culinary amounts.

name: Panch phoron
description: Five whole seeds thrown into hot oil together — fenugreek, nigella, cumin, fennel, mustard.

tcm.note: Whole aromatic seeds, all warming.

ayurveda.note: Ushna, though the fennel in it pulls gently the other way.

unani.note: Garam-khushk; a tempering blend by design.

histamine.note: Very low.

name: Black vinegar
description: Malty dark rice vinegar aged in jars — the dipping vinegar for dumplings.

tcm.note: Cu is warm, sour and astringent; it enters the liver and moves stagnation.

ayurveda.note: Shukta is ushna.

histamine.note: Aged for months to years — unlike plain rice vinegar, this one earns the high rating.

name: Dark soy sauce
description: Soy sauce aged longer with molasses — used for colour more than salt.

tcm.note: Long-fermented and sweetened.

ayurveda.note: Fermented and salty, so ushna.

histamine.note: A longer ferment than light soy — same mechanism, more of it.

name: Mirin
description: Sweet fermented rice liquor used for glazing rather than drinking.

tcm.note: Read with rice wine, which is warm and qi-moving.

ayurveda.note: Madya-adjacent, so ushna.

histamine.note: Fermented and alcoholic — cooking it off removes the alcohol, not the histamine.

name: Worcestershire sauce
description: Anchovies, tamarind and molasses fermented for eighteen months.

tcm.note: Fermented, salty and sour; no classical entry.

ayurveda.note: Ushna by ferment and sourness.

histamine.note: Fermented anchovy base aged for over a year — high, and hidden in marinades and Bloody Marys.

name: Dukkah
description: Crushed nuts, sesame and coriander — bread is dipped in oil, then in this.

tcm.note: Toasted nuts and warm seeds.

ayurveda.note: Ushna and guru from the nuts.

histamine.note: Nut-based, so it carries the nut liberator flags — hazelnut and peanut versions differ.

name: Shawarma spice
description: Cumin, coriander, paprika, cinnamon and clove — the rub on the vertical spit.

tcm.note: Every component is warming.

ayurveda.note: Ushna throughout.

histamine.note: Paprika-heavy, and the dried capsicums are liberators.

name: Vanilla
description: Cured orchid pods, or the alcohol extract drawn from them.

tcm.note: A new-world spice; aromatic and read as gently warming.

ayurveda.note: Ushna by its aroma; no classical entry.

histamine.note: Low in the amounts used. The pods are cured for months, but a teaspoon of extract is a teaspoon.

name: Cornstarch
description: Pure corn starch — the slurry that thickens a Chinese sauce.

tcm.note: Follows corn, which is neutral.

ayurveda.note: Shita and heavy; pure starch with nothing else in it.

histamine.note: Very low — one of the safest thickeners on a reactive day.

name: Brown sugar
description: White sugar with some molasses left in or added back.

tcm.note: Hong tang is warm in TCM and given for cold-type period pain — unlike white sugar, which is cool.

ayurveda.note: Closer to guda (jaggery) than to refined sugar, so ushna.

histamine.note: Low.

name: Stevia
description: Leaf-derived sweetener with no sugar and no calories.

tcm.note: A modern isolate; the leaf is read as cooling.

ayurveda.note: Madhura in taste without the substance; no classical entry.

histamine.note: Low; some people react to the leaf extract independently of histamine.

name: Raw honey
description: Unheated, unfiltered honey — still carrying pollen and wax.

tcm.note: Feng mi is neutral-to-warm, moistens dryness and harmonises other herbs.

ayurveda.note: Madhu is ushna despite being sweet, and classically must never be heated — the one rule everyone knows.

unani.note: Garam-khushk; a standard Unani vehicle for warming medicines.

histamine.note: Low, though pollen content means it can set off pollen-allergic people through a different route.

name: Sonth
description: Ginger dried and ground — hotter and drier than the fresh root, and used differently.

tcm.note: Gan jiang is hot where fresh sheng jiang is only warm — it warms the interior rather than releasing the exterior.

ayurveda.note: Shunthi is ushna and drier than ardraka; a classical digestive and postpartum drug.

histamine.note: Very low.

name: Cayenne pepper
description: Finely ground hot dried chilli, used for heat rather than flavour.

tcm.note: Read with chilli — hot and dispersing.

ayurveda.note: Katu and ushna in a high degree.

histamine.note: Dried capsicums are liberators.

name: Garlic powder
description: Dehydrated ground garlic — convenient, and quite unlike the fresh clove.

tcm.note: Read with garlic.

ayurveda.note: Lashuna is ushna and tikshna.

histamine.note: Low.

nutrition.highlight: not the same as a clove

name: Onion powder
description: Dehydrated ground onion, used where fresh would add water.

tcm.note: Read with onion.

ayurveda.note: Palandu is ushna.

histamine.note: Low.

name: Chilli flakes
description: Coarsely crushed dried chilli with the seeds left in.

tcm.note: Read with chilli.

ayurveda.note: Ushna and tikshna.

histamine.note: Dried capsicum liberator.

name: Ras el hanout
description: A shop's best blend — sometimes thirty spices, and no two the same.

tcm.note: Read from its components; warming throughout.

ayurveda.note: Ushna by all its parts.

histamine.note: Low in culinary amounts.

name: Berbere
description: Fiery Ethiopian blend of chilli, fenugreek, ajwain and warm spice.

tcm.note: Chilli-led and warming throughout.

ayurveda.note: Ushna in a high degree.

histamine.note: Chilli-heavy.

name: Tandoori masala
description: The red rub for anything going into a tandoor — chilli, garam masala and colour.

tcm.note: Chilli and warm spice.

ayurveda.note: Ushna throughout.

histamine.note: Chilli- and paprika-heavy.

name: Biryani masala
description: Whole-spice-heavy blend built on cardamom, mace and bay for layered rice.

tcm.note: Aromatic and warming.

ayurveda.note: Ushna.

histamine.note: Low in culinary amounts.

name: Pav bhaji masala
description: Sour-hot blend with amchur and black salt, made for one dish and used in many.

tcm.note: Sour and chilli-forward.

ayurveda.note: Ushna.

histamine.note: Amchur-based.

name: Rasam powder
description: Coriander, pepper, cumin and dal roasted and ground for rasam.

tcm.note: Pepper-led.

ayurveda.note: Ushna and deepana.

histamine.note: Low in culinary amounts.

name: Milagai podi
description: Roasted dal and chilli ground coarse, mixed with sesame oil beside idli.

tcm.note: Roasted chilli and dal.

ayurveda.note: Ushna and tikshna.

histamine.note: Chilli-heavy.

name: Gochugaru
description: Coarse sun-dried Korean chilli — bright red, fruity and only moderately hot.

tcm.note: Read with chilli.

ayurveda.note: Ushna and tikshna.

histamine.note: Dried capsicum liberator.

name: Doubanjiang
description: Broad beans and chilli fermented for months to years — the soul of Sichuan cooking.

tcm.note: Fermented and chilli-led — hot and dispersing.

ayurveda.note: Ushna in a high degree.

histamine.note: Months to years of bean ferment plus chilli — both mechanisms, in quantity.

name: XO sauce
description: Dried scallop and shrimp fried with chilli and ham into a luxury condiment.

tcm.note: Dried seafood, chilli and cured ham.

ayurveda.note: Ushna in a high degree.

histamine.note: Dried seafood and cured ham together — about as high as a condiment gets.

name: Shrimp paste
description: Shrimp salted and fermented into a dense grey block with a formidable smell.

tcm.note: Fermented seafood; warming.

ayurveda.note: Ushna in a high degree.

histamine.note: Fermented shellfish — among the very highest-histamine ingredients in any kitchen.

name: Dried shrimp
description: Tiny shrimp salted and sun-dried, pounded into pastes and sambals.

tcm.note: Read with shrimp; drying concentrates it.

ayurveda.note: Ushna in a high degree.

histamine.note: Dried and salted shellfish — both the shellfish liberator flag and a heavy amine load.

name: Kasundi
description: Bengali fermented mustard condiment — pungent enough to clear the sinuses.

tcm.note: Mustard, fermented.

ayurveda.note: Sarshapa is ushna and tikshna; fermenting adds to it.

histamine.note: A traditional ferment on a mustard base.

name: Ginger garlic paste
description: Equal ginger and garlic ground together — the first thing into most desi pans.

tcm.note: Both components are warm to hot and dispersing.

ayurveda.note: Ushna and tikshna.

histamine.note: Low fresh. Jarred versions carry preservatives and sit for months, which is different.

nutrition.highlight: the first thing in the pan

name: Baking soda
description: Sodium bicarbonate — raises batters, tenderises meat, and softens chickpeas.

tcm.note: Alkaline and mineral; read with the salts, which are cold in TCM.

ayurveda.note: Kshara (alkali) is classically ushna and tikshna.

unani.note: Sajji is garam-khushk in the Unani record — an alkali used to cut phlegm.

histamine.note: None.

name: Baking powder
description: Bicarbonate with an acid already blended in, so it works without buttermilk.

tcm.note: Read with baking soda.

ayurveda.note: Kshara-adjacent; no classical entry.

histamine.note: None.

name: Yeast
description: The living organism that raises bread — dried, fresh or as a nutritional flake.

tcm.note: A leavening organism rather than a food; read as warming and fermenting.

ayurveda.note: Fermentation is ushna.

unani.note: Khameer is garam in the Unani record.

histamine.note: Baker's yeast in a risen loaf is usually tolerated; yeast extract and nutritional yeast are concentrated and much higher — SIGHI treats them very differently.

name: Gelatin
description: Collagen extracted from hides and bones — what sets a jelly.

tcm.note: A rendered animal product; read with the bone preparations.

ayurveda.note: Ushna and guru, in the mamsa group.

histamine.note: Made from long-processed connective tissue, like the broths.

name: Agar
description: Seaweed-derived setting agent that sets firmer than gelatin and needs no chilling.

tcm.note: Read with the seaweeds, which are cold and softening.

ayurveda.note: Shita; used in cooling desserts.

histamine.note: Low — and the vegetarian setting agent for anyone avoiding gelatin.

name: Almond extract
description: Bitter almond oil in alcohol — a few drops flavour a whole cake.

tcm.note: Read with the apricot kernel it usually comes from.

ayurveda.note: Ushna.

histamine.note: Low; used in drops.

name: Vanaspati
description: Hydrogenated vegetable oil made to imitate ghee — the fat behind most commercial mithai.

tcm.note: A modern industrial fat with no classical entry.

ayurveda.note: Ushna and very guru; classically nothing like the ghee it imitates.

histamine.note: Low for histamine. Its trans-fat content is the real and separate concern.

name: Dashi
description: Kombu and bonito steeped briefly — the savoury base under almost all Japanese cooking.

tcm.note: Kelp is cold; the bonito warms it. Net cooling, and very light.

ayurveda.note: Outside the classical record; a sea-vegetable broth, read as shita.

unani.note: Outside the classical record; placed with the sea vegetables.

histamine.note: Both its ingredients are among the highest on the SIGHI list — dried seaweed and mould-fermented fish. It is under almost everything Japanese, which is worth knowing.

name: Kinako
description: Roasted soybean flour dusted over mochi and stirred into milk.

tcm.note: Read with soy; roasting adds warmth.

ayurveda.note: Shita, following the soybean.

unani.note: Outside the classical record; placed with soy.

histamine.note: Low — unfermented soy.

name: Takuan
description: Daikon salted and fermented for months until it turns yellow and rubbery.

tcm.note: Read with radish, which is cool and descending; the ferment warms it.

ayurveda.note: Soured and salted, so ushna.

unani.note: Outside the classical record; garam by its cure.

histamine.note: A months-long vegetable ferment, like kimchi and sauerkraut.

name: Tsukemono
description: The pickle plate — anything from a quick salt-press to a year in rice bran.

tcm.note: Mostly cooling vegetables; the cure warms them.

ayurveda.note: Salted and soured, so ushna.

unani.note: Outside the classical record; garam by cure.

histamine.note: Rated for the fermented kind. A same-day salt-press (asazuke) is far lower — the two are served on the same plate and rarely distinguished.

nutrition.highlight: a same-day press, or a year in bran

name: Hijiki
description: Black shredded seaweed rehydrated and simmered with soy and carrot.

tcm.note: With the cooling sea vegetables.

ayurveda.note: Outside the classical record; read with kelp and nori.

unani.note: Outside the classical record; placed with the seaweeds.

histamine.note: Dried sea vegetable. It also carries inorganic arsenic, which is a separate and real caution.

name: Doenjang
description: Soybeans fermented in brine for months to years — earthier and saltier than miso.

tcm.note: A long salty ferment; warming and descending.

ayurveda.note: Fermented and salty, so ushna.

unani.note: Outside the classical record; garam by ferment and salt.

histamine.note: Years of ferment in some households — higher again than miso.

name: Ganjang
description: Korean soy sauce — the soup kind is saltier and paler than the Chinese sort.

tcm.note: Fermented and salty.

ayurveda.note: Ushna by ferment.

unani.note: Outside the classical record; garam by ferment.

histamine.note: Fermented soy, like all soy sauces.

nutrition.highlight: the soup kind is paler, and saltier

name: Ssamjang
description: Doenjang and gochujang mixed with sesame and garlic — the sauce inside a lettuce wrap.

tcm.note: Two ferments plus chilli and garlic.

ayurveda.note: Ushna and tikshna.

histamine.note: Two fermented pastes at once, plus chilli.

name: Cheonggukjang
description: Soybeans fermented for two or three days into a pungent sticky paste — Korea's natto.

tcm.note: A short intense ferment.

ayurveda.note: Ushna by ferment.

unani.note: Outside the classical record; garam by ferment.

histamine.note: A bacillus ferment like natto — high, and famous for its smell.

name: Jeotgal
description: Seafood salted and fermented for months — the umami engine inside kimchi.

tcm.note: Fermented salted seafood.

ayurveda.note: Ushna in a high degree.

histamine.note: Fermented seafood — among the very highest, and it is what makes kimchi taste like kimchi.

name: Saeujeot
description: Tiny shrimp packed in salt and left to break down — used by the spoonful.

tcm.note: Salted fermented shellfish.

ayurveda.note: Ushna in a high degree.

histamine.note: Fermented shellfish: both the liberator flag and a heavy amine load.

name: Dashida
description: Powdered beef-and-vegetable stock base found in most Korean kitchens.

tcm.note: Outside the classical record; a modern stock powder; read as warming.

ayurveda.note: Outside the classical record; ushna by its meat base and salt.

histamine.note: Concentrated meat extract with yeast extract — both high, and it is in a great many home dishes.

name: Perilla leaf
description: Broad minty-anise leaf used for wrapping — related to shiso, but not the same.

tcm.note: Zi su ye is warm and releases the exterior; a classical drug for chills and fish.

ayurveda.note: Katu and ushna by its aroma.

unani.note: Outside the classical record; aromatic leaves read as warming.

histamine.note: Very low.

nutrition.highlight: related to shiso, not the same

name: Pandan
description: Long green leaf knotted into rice and syrups — the vanilla of Southeast Asia.

tcm.note: Outside the classical record; an aromatic leaf; read as cooling and fragrance-releasing.

ayurveda.note: Ketaki-family; shita and used the way rose is.

histamine.note: Very low.

name: Holy basil
description: Peppery clove-scented basil — the leaf that makes pad krapow what it is.

tcm.note: Aromatic and dispersing.

ayurveda.note: Tulsi is ushna, katu and tikta — a classical rasayana for the chest.

unani.note: Garam-khushk; used against cough and cold.

histamine.note: Very low.

nutrition.highlight: not the same as sweet basil

name: Bird's eye chilli
description: Small chillies with heat far out of proportion to their size.

tcm.note: Read with chilli — hot and dispersing in the extreme.

ayurveda.note: Katu and ushna in the highest degree.

histamine.note: Capsicums are liberators; fresh is lower than dried.

name: Krachai
description: Finger-shaped rhizome, medicinal and camphorous — used in jungle curries and fish dishes.

tcm.note: Read with the ginger family; warming and dispersing.

ayurveda.note: Ushna and katu, in the ardraka group.

histamine.note: Very low.

name: Coriander root
description: The root of the coriander plant, pounded into curry pastes — earthier than the leaf.

tcm.note: Read with coriander, which is cooling and fragrance-releasing.

ayurveda.note: Dhanyaka is shita and deepana.

unani.note: Thanda; the whole plant is cooling in Unani usage.

histamine.note: Very low.

name: Rau ram
description: Sharp peppery leaf eaten raw in Vietnamese salads and soups.

tcm.note: Outside the classical record; pungent aromatic leaf; read as warming.

ayurveda.note: Outside the classical record; katu and read as ushna.

unani.note: Outside the classical record; placed with the pungent herbs.

histamine.note: Very low.

name: Ngo gai
description: Long serrated leaf with a coriander flavour several times stronger.

tcm.note: Outside the classical record; read with coriander, which it tastes of.

ayurveda.note: Outside the classical record; shita, with the coriander family.

unani.note: Outside the classical record; placed with coriander.

histamine.note: Very low.

name: Laksa leaf
description: The defining herb of curry laksa — hot, citrusy and faintly soapy.

tcm.note: Outside the classical record; pungent aromatic; read as warming.

ayurveda.note: Outside the classical record; katu and ushna.

unani.note: Outside the classical record; placed with the pungent herbs.

histamine.note: Very low.

name: Torch ginger
description: Pink ginger flower bud shredded raw into salads and asam laksa.

tcm.note: Outside the classical record; a flower bud; milder and cooler than the rhizome.

ayurveda.note: Outside the classical record; read with the ginger family, though far gentler.

unani.note: Outside the classical record; placed with ginger.

histamine.note: Very low.

name: Salam leaf
description: Indonesian bay leaf — related to neither bay nor curry leaf, and milder than both.

tcm.note: Outside the classical record; an aromatic leaf, read with bay.

ayurveda.note: Outside the classical record; ushna by aroma.

unani.note: Outside the classical record; placed with bay leaf.

histamine.note: Very low.

name: Young ginger
description: Pale pink-tipped ginger before the skin toughens — juicy, mild, barely fibrous.

tcm.note: Sheng jiang is warm and releases the exterior; the young root is gentler.

ayurveda.note: Ardraka is ushna, if milder when young.

histamine.note: Very low.

name: Fresh turmeric
description: The raw rhizome — earthier and more bitter than the dried powder, and it stains everything.

tcm.note: Jiang huang is warm, moves blood and breaks stagnation.

ayurveda.note: Haridra is ushna, katu and tikta — a classical blood purifier.

histamine.note: Very low.

name: Siling labuyo
description: The small fierce Filipino chilli, used whole in stews and crushed into vinegar.

tcm.note: Read with chilli.

ayurveda.note: Katu and ushna in a high degree.

histamine.note: Capsicum liberator.

nutrition.highlight: used whole, or crushed in vinegar

name: Dried chilli
description: Whole chillies dried until leathery, soaked before pounding into paste.

tcm.note: Read with chilli; drying concentrates it.

ayurveda.note: Ushna in a high degree.

histamine.note: Dried capsicums rate above fresh — the drying concentrates the amines too.

name: Keluak
description: A nut that is lethally toxic fresh and edible only after months of burial and fermentation.

tcm.note: Outside the classical record; a long-fermented seed; read as warming.

ayurveda.note: Outside the classical record; fermented, so ushna.

unani.note: Outside the classical record; garam by ferment.

histamine.note: Months of deliberate fermentation — and the raw nut contains cyanide, which the burial is there to remove.

nutrition.highlight: buried for months to make it safe

name: Palm sugar
description: Sap from palm flowers boiled to a soft dark sugar — smokier than cane.

tcm.note: Read with jaggery, which is warm and building.

ayurveda.note: Guda is ushna.

histamine.note: Low.

name: Kecap manis
description: Soy sauce thickened with palm sugar into a dark syrup.

tcm.note: Fermented soy, sweetened.

ayurveda.note: Ushna by ferment and sugar.

unani.note: Outside the classical record; garam by ferment.

histamine.note: Fermented soy base.

name: Sambal oelek
description: Chillies ground with salt and a little vinegar — heat with nothing else in the way.

tcm.note: Pure chilli; hot and dispersing.

ayurveda.note: Katu and ushna in the highest degree.

histamine.note: Chilli liberator plus vinegar. Lower than fermented sambals, which climb further.

nutrition.highlight: heat, with nothing in the way

name: Nam prik pao
description: Roasted chilli, shallot and garlic cooked into a sweet dark jam with shrimp paste.

tcm.note: Roasted chilli and allium in oil.

ayurveda.note: Ushna in a high degree.

histamine.note: Shrimp paste and dried shrimp in the base — fermented seafood plus chilli.

name: Red curry paste
description: Dried red chilli pounded with lemongrass, galangal and shrimp paste.

tcm.note: Chilli, galangal and pepper together — hot throughout.

ayurveda.note: Ushna and tikshna.

histamine.note: Shrimp paste in the base makes every Thai curry paste high, however fresh the herbs.

nutrition.highlight: shrimp paste is in nearly all of them

name: Green curry paste
description: Fresh green chilli pounded with coriander root, kaffir zest and shrimp paste.

tcm.note: Fresh chilli-led; hot and dispersing.

ayurveda.note: Ushna and tikshna.

histamine.note: Shrimp paste base.

name: Massaman paste
description: A Persian-influenced paste with cinnamon, clove and cardamom alongside the chilli.

tcm.note: Warm whole spices over a milder chilli base.

ayurveda.note: Ushna throughout.

unani.note: Garam-khushk — the most Unani-looking of the Thai pastes.

histamine.note: Shrimp paste base.

name: Panang paste
description: A red paste with peanuts ground in — thicker and sweeter than the others.

tcm.note: Chilli with peanut; rich and warming.

ayurveda.note: Ushna.

histamine.note: Shrimp paste plus peanuts — two liberator sources.

name: Yellow curry paste
description: Turmeric-led paste closest to an Indian curry, and the mildest of the Thai set.

tcm.note: Turmeric and cumin over mild chilli.

ayurveda.note: Haridra and jiraka are both ushna.

histamine.note: Shrimp paste base.

name: Khao khua
description: Sticky rice dry-toasted and ground — the nutty grit in larb.

tcm.note: Dry-roasted grain; warming and drying.

ayurveda.note: Ushna and ruksha from the roasting.

histamine.note: Very low.

name: Patis
description: Filipino fish sauce — the liquid drawn off fermenting bagoong.

tcm.note: Fermented fish; salty and warming.

ayurveda.note: Ushna in a high degree.

histamine.note: Fermented fish — among the highest condiments there are.

name: Bagoong
description: Fermented shrimp or fish paste, pink and pungent, fried before use.

tcm.note: Fermented salted seafood.

ayurveda.note: Ushna in a high degree.

histamine.note: Fermented shellfish.

name: Banana ketchup
description: Banana purée dyed red and soured — a wartime substitute that stayed.

tcm.note: Outside the classical record; banana is cold; the vinegar and sugar warm it.

ayurveda.note: Outside the classical record; soured and sweetened, so ushna.

unani.note: Outside the classical record; garam by its vinegar.

histamine.note: Vinegar-based, and banana carries a liberator flag.

name: Coconut vinegar
description: Cloudy vinegar from fermented coconut sap — the Filipino souring agent.

tcm.note: Cu is warm, sour and astringent.

ayurveda.note: Shukta is ushna.

histamine.note: Fermented twice, like other vinegars.

name: Annatto
description: Brick-red seeds steeped in oil for colour — barely any flavour of its own.

tcm.note: Outside the classical record; used for colour; no classical entry.

ayurveda.note: Outside the classical record; read as mildly ushna.

unani.note: Outside the classical record; outside the record.

histamine.note: Low; used in tiny amounts for colour.

name: Fried shallots
description: Shallots sliced paper-thin and fried crisp — scattered over almost everything.

tcm.note: Allium, fried; warming.

ayurveda.note: Ushna and tikshna.

histamine.note: Low. They go rancid quickly, which is a fat problem rather than histamine.

name: Do chua
description: Julienned carrot and radish in sweet vinegar — the crunch inside a banh mi.

tcm.note: Raw root vegetables; the vinegar warms them.

ayurveda.note: Soured, so ushna.

unani.note: Outside the classical record; thanda by the vegetables, garam by the vinegar.

histamine.note: A quick vinegar pickle, not a long ferment — lower than kimchi or sauerkraut.

nutrition.highlight: the crunch inside a banh mi

name: Coconut cream
description: The thick first pressing of grated coconut — richer than coconut milk.

tcm.note: Outside the classical record; read with coconut.

ayurveda.note: Narikela is shita, guru and snigdha.

histamine.note: Low; it sours fast once opened.

name: Jalapeño
description: Thick-walled green chilli with moderate heat — the default fresh chilli of Mexico.

tcm.note: Read with chilli — hot and dispersing.

ayurveda.note: Katu and ushna.

histamine.note: Capsicum liberator; pickled jalapeños rate higher again.

name: Serrano chilli
description: Thinner and hotter than jalapeño, used raw in salsas.

tcm.note: Read with chilli.

ayurveda.note: Ushna in a high degree.

histamine.note: Capsicum liberator.

name: Habanero
description: Lantern-shaped chilli, fruity and ferociously hot.

tcm.note: Among the hottest of the capsicums.

ayurveda.note: Ushna in the highest degree.

histamine.note: Capsicum liberator.

name: Poblano
description: Large mild dark-green chilli, roasted and peeled for rellenos.

tcm.note: A mild capsicum; warming rather than hot.

ayurveda.note: Ushna, gently.

histamine.note: Capsicum liberator, though mild.

name: Chipotle
description: Jalapeño smoked and dried, usually sold in a vinegary adobo sauce.

tcm.note: Smoked and dried chilli.

ayurveda.note: Ushna in a high degree.

histamine.note: Smoked, dried and packed in vinegar — three processes that each raise it.

name: Ancho chilli
description: Dried poblano — raisiny and mild, the backbone of most moles.

tcm.note: Dried mild chilli.

ayurveda.note: Ushna.

histamine.note: Dried capsicum.

name: Guajillo
description: Long dried red chilli with a tangy berry note — the other half of most moles.

tcm.note: Dried chilli.

ayurveda.note: Ushna.

histamine.note: Dried capsicum.

nutrition.highlight: the other half of a mole

name: Ají amarillo
description: Fruity orange chilli, the defining heat of Peruvian cooking.

tcm.note: Read with chilli.

ayurveda.note: Ushna.

histamine.note: Capsicum liberator.

name: Rocoto
description: Thick-fleshed chilli with black seeds — looks like a pepper, bites like a habanero.

tcm.note: Among the hotter capsicums.

ayurveda.note: Ushna in a high degree.

histamine.note: Capsicum liberator.

name: Epazote
description: Pungent herb added to beans — traditionally to reduce the wind they cause.

tcm.note: Outside the classical record; pungent and carminative; read as warming.

ayurveda.note: Katu and ushna, and deepana — the same reasoning as ajwain.

histamine.note: Very low; used in small amounts.

nutrition.highlight: added to beans, for the wind

name: Mexican oregano
description: Not related to Mediterranean oregano — more citrus, less mint.

tcm.note: Outside the classical record; aromatic and warming, like the herb it is named after.

ayurveda.note: Outside the classical record; katu and ushna.

histamine.note: Very low.

nutrition.highlight: not related to the other oregano

name: Canela
description: Soft brittle true cinnamon — sweeter and less fierce than cassia.

tcm.note: Rou gui is warm and warms the interior; the softer bark is gentler.

ayurveda.note: Twak is ushna and deepana.

histamine.note: Very low.

name: Piloncillo
description: Unrefined cane sugar set in cones — the Latin American gur.

tcm.note: Read with jaggery, which is warm and building.

ayurveda.note: Guda is ushna.

histamine.note: Low.

name: Huacatay
description: Marigold-family herb with a mint-and-basil smell, ground into Andean sauces.

tcm.note: Outside the classical record; aromatic and pungent; read as warming.

ayurveda.note: Outside the classical record; katu and ushna.

unani.note: Outside the classical record; outside the record.

histamine.note: Very low.

name: Dendê oil
description: Unrefined red palm oil — the colour and smell of Bahian cooking.

tcm.note: Outside the classical record; read with palm oil; heavy and warming.

ayurveda.note: Outside the classical record; ushna and very guru.

histamine.note: Low as a fat.

name: Dried lime
description: Limes boiled in brine and sun-dried until hollow and black — pierced and dropped whole into stews.

tcm.note: Outside the classical record; dried sour citrus; read with the citrus family.

ayurveda.note: Amla-rasa is ushna; drying concentrates it.

unani.note: Thanda-khushk in Gulf usage, taken against bilious heat.

histamine.note: Dried and concentrated sour citrus.

name: Advieh
description: Rose petal, cardamom, cinnamon and cumin ground together — floral rather than hot.

tcm.note: Warm aromatics throughout.

ayurveda.note: Ushna, though the rose pulls the other way.

histamine.note: Low in culinary amounts.

name: Pul biber
description: Coarse oily red flakes with more fruit than fire — on every Turkish table.

tcm.note: Read with chilli, though mild.

ayurveda.note: Katu and ushna.

histamine.note: Dried capsicum liberator.

name: Urfa biber
description: Chilli sweated in the sun then wrapped at night, turning almost black and raisiny.

tcm.note: Dried and sweated chilli.

ayurveda.note: Ushna.

histamine.note: Dried capsicum; the sweating process is not a ferment.

nutrition.highlight: sweated by day, wrapped by night

name: Mahleb
description: Ground cherry kernels with a bitter-almond scent, used in Levantine and Turkish baking.

tcm.note: Outside the classical record; read with the apricot kernel, its closest documented relative.

ayurveda.note: Outside the classical record; ushna by aroma.

histamine.note: Low; used in pinches.

name: Mastic
description: Resin tears from the mastic tree, pounded and used for their pine-resin scent and chew.

tcm.note: An aromatic resin; warming and drying.

ayurveda.note: Outside the classical record; read with the aromatic resins.

unani.note: Mastaki is garam-khushk in Unani and given for the stomach.

histamine.note: Very low; used in tiny amounts.

name: Pekmez
description: Grape juice boiled down to a dark syrup — eaten with tahini for breakfast.

tcm.note: Concentrated grape must.

ayurveda.note: Draksha is shita even reduced.

unani.note: Garam-tar; a strengthening winter food in the Unani record.

histamine.note: Concentrated grape — grapes carry more amines than most fruit.

name: Verjuice
description: The pressed juice of unripe grapes — sour without the fermentation of vinegar.

tcm.note: Sour unripe fruit; cooling.

ayurveda.note: Amla-rasa is ushna.

unani.note: Ab ghooreh is barid in the Unani record, used specifically to cool bilious heat.

histamine.note: Sour, but crucially not fermented — it is the low-histamine alternative to vinegar.

name: Tarragon
description: Aniseed-scented herb eaten raw by the bunch on a Persian table.

tcm.note: Outside the classical record; aromatic and warming; thin Chinese record.

ayurveda.note: Katu and ushna by aroma.

unani.note: Tarkhun is garam-khushk in the Unani record, a carminative.

histamine.note: Very low.

name: Summer savory
description: Peppery thyme-like herb, dried into Persian and Turkish blends.

tcm.note: Outside the classical record; read with thyme, which it resembles.

ayurveda.note: Outside the classical record; katu and ushna.

histamine.note: Very low.
